content.text: The clause meets the preferred position: Customer may terminate without cause on 30 days' notice (via §29.4) with refund of prepaid Fees, and Vendor has no convenience right.

input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 gives Customer an unconditional termination-for-convenience right over the Agreement or any Order Form, and the cross-referenced Section 29.4 fixes the notice period at "thirty days before the effective termination date" — matching the preferred 30 days' written notice. There is no early-termination fee or unwinding penalty: Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (reinforced by Section 10.2, which requires refund of prepaid recurring Fees). This is the preferred pro-rata refund outcome. On the other side of the direction test, the three-year term in Section 8.1 is not paired with any Vendor convenience right: Vendor's termination rights are limited to mutual material breach (9.1) and insolvency (9.2), Section 20.5/p0087 expressly bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services, and Section 24.4 blocks Vendor termination on Customer change of control. A search for "convenience" returns only an unrelated Order Form definition. Accordingly the clause sits at the preferred position on every material term (notice length, refund, no penalty, no Vendor mid-term walk-away) and no redline is warranted.
